findings.description: The magic-link token is built with `random.choices`, which uses the Mersenne Twister. Its output is predictable once enough values have been observed. The token alone authenticates a member and starts a session, so an attacker who can request links, or who sees other tokens, could predict a valid token and take over accounts.
findings.suggestion: Use the `secrets` module, e.g. `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)` or `"".join(secrets.choice(_TOKEN_ALPHABET) for _ in range(TOKEN_LENGTH))`.
findings.title: Sign-in token generated with non-cryptographic PRNG

findings.description: `redeem` pops the pending link and starts a session without comparing `link.expires_at` with `now`. Expired links remain valid until `purge_expired` happens to run, so a link emailed long ago still signs the user in, despite the email promising a 15-minute expiry.
findings.suggestion: After popping, `if link.expires_at <= now: raise LinkRejected(...)`.
findings.title: Expiry is never checked when redeeming a link
